answer.rationale: A release went out 2 hours ago coinciding with p99 latency climbing 5x target during peak settlement traffic. Memory_b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact. Memory_b6 shows staged release gating can catch regressions. With exactly one intervention capacity and writes being heavy at settlement peak, rolling back the recent release is the fastest path to restore latency stability. This preserves the transactional write path during peak load without requiring orchestration across failover or capacity changes. If the release is not the root cause, the rollback will be inconclusive but quickly reversible, allowing escalation to other options in the next window.
